content.title: About
content.content: Infant formula is a nutritious dry powder designed for babies from birth to 12 months. It is sold under the store brand, has a gentle taste, and is prepared using specially purified baby water (361).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula provides all essential macro‑ and micronutrients for infant growth.
It often includes prebiotics and probiotics to support gut microbiota.
Formulas can be tailored: hypoallergenic, lactose‑free, with added DHA and ARA.
Typical packaging is 400‑600 g, yielding about 30‑40 servings.
When stored correctly, the formula retains its quality for up to 2 years.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: The formula offers an optimal balance of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals needed for brain and physical development.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Contains calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin D to promote strong bone formation.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, E and zinc help strengthen the infant’s immune system.

items.title: Gut health
items.content: Pre‑ and probiotics foster beneficial gut flora, reducing the risk of constipation.

items.title: Vision development
items.content: Added DHA and ARA support retinal and neural development for healthy eyesight.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some infants may be allergic to cow‑milk protein or other ingredients in the formula.

items.title: Improper reconstitution
items.content: Over‑concentrated mixtures can strain kidneys, while overly diluted ones may not provide enough energy.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the powder should be used within 1‑2 months to maintain quality.

items.title: Water contamination
items.content: Only use the specially purified baby water (361) and clean utensils to avoid bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: For one serving (≈150 ml), add 7 g of powder to 150 ml of warm (not hot) baby water (361) and stir until smooth. Let the mixture cool to body temperature before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry powder in its original airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the lid tightly sealed.

content.title: About
content.content: Olives are the fruit of the olive tree (Olea europaea), native to the Mediterranean region and other areas with a mild climate. They come in green and black varieties, depending on ripeness and processing method. Olives are eaten after brining and are also used in cooking, oil production, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Olive trees can live for more than 1,000 years, with some specimens exceeding 2,000 years.
The oldest archaeological evidence of olives dates back to 7,000 BC.
Olive oil is a cornerstone of the Mediterranean diet.
Green olives are harvested before full ripeness, while black olives are picked after they fully mature.
In ancient Rome, olives symbolized peace and victory.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Olives contain oleic acid, which supports cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Olives provide polyphenols such as oleuropein that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Olives contain calcium, magnesium, and vitamin K, which contribute to bone strength.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E in olives helps shield cells from free‑radical damage.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The fiber in olives promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Brined olives often contain a lot of salt, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Olive allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to olives.

items.title: Oleuropein content
items.content: In large amounts, oleuropein can cause gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Olives are calorie‑dense due to their fat content, so they should be consumed in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Olives can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, pastas, pizza, tapenade, and fish dishes. They are also the source for olive oil. Before eating, olives are usually rinsed to remove excess brine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store olives in an airtight jar in the refrigerator, submerged in brine. Properly stored, they keep for several months. Discard olives that show mold or an off smell.

content.title: About
content.content: Passion fruit (Passiflora edulis) is the fruit of a tropical vine, native to South America. The fruits are round or oval, with a tough purple or yellow rind that wrinkles as it ripens. Inside is aromatic, jelly-like pulp with crunchy edible seeds, tart and sweet in flavor. Passion fruit is eaten fresh and added to desserts, juices, sauces, and cocktails.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name passion fruit comes from the word passion: missionaries saw the flower as a symbol of the Passion of Christ.
There are purple and yellow passion fruits.
The fruit is considered ripe when its rind becomes wrinkled.
Brazil is one of the largest producers of passion fruit.
Passion fruit seeds are edible and crunchy.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and helps you feel full.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and skin.

items.title: Contains carotenoids
items.content: The body partly converts carotenoids into vitamin A.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains polyphenols
items.content: The polyphenols in passion fruit have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Passion fruit can cause allergic reactions, including in people with latex allergy.

items.title: Rind and unripe fruit
items.content: The rind and unripe fruit contain cyanogenic compounds, so the rind is not eaten and it is better to choose ripe fruit.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Passion fruit is acidic and may cause heartburn or irritate tooth enamel.

items.title: Sugar in juices and desserts
items.content: Ready-made passion fruit juices, syrups, and desserts often contain a lot of added sugar.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut a ripe passion fruit in half and eat the pulp with a spoon, seeds included. Add the pulp to yogurt, smoothies, desserts, sauces, and cocktails; the juice can be strained to remove the seeds. Do not eat the rind.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Leave firm fruit at room temperature to ripen. Store ripe fruit in the refrigerator for one to two weeks. The pulp can be frozen.

shrimp-chow-mein-or-chop-suey-no-noodles.title: Shrimp Chow Mein (or Chop Suey) without Noodles

content.title: About
content.content: The dish is a stir‑fried mix of shrimp, vegetables (bell pepper, carrot, onion, broccoli) and soy‑based sauce, prepared without the traditional noodles. It retains the savory Asian flavor while being lower in carbohydrates.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Often offered in restaurants as a low‑carb alternative to classic chow mein.
Shrimp are an excellent source of protein and omega‑3 fatty acids.
Traditional chow‑mein sauce is made from soy sauce, oyster sauce, ginger and garlic.
Skipping the noodles reduces the carb count to about 5–7 g per serving, helpful for blood‑sugar control.
In China a similar dish is called “chop suey” – a mix of meat and vegetables without grains.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide roughly 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: Without noodles the dish contains only 5–7 g of carbs per serving, suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Source of omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids promote cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables contribute vitamin C, vitamin K, folate and potassium.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: One portion is about 180 kcal, making it a good option for weight management.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Shrimp can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce is often high in salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you have hypertension.

items.title: Foodborne pathogens
items.content: Improperly cooked shrimp may harbor bacteria that cause food poisoning.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: A large amount of raw vegetables can cause gas in people with sensitive guts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, optionally over rice or as a standalone meal. Squeeze fresh lemon, add chili flakes or sprinkle toasted sesame seeds for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave, adding a splash of water to prevent drying out.

content.title: About
content.content: Sun-dried tomatoes are ripe tomatoes that have been dried in the sun or a dehydrator until most of the moisture is removed. They have a concentrated sweet‑tart flavor, a dense chewy texture, and a vivid red color. Sun-dried tomatoes are a staple of Mediterranean cuisine, used in salads, pastas, pizzas, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional production occurs in Mediterranean regions where the climate allows natural dehydration.
Sugar content can reach up to 30 % of their weight, making them naturally sweet without added sugar.
They are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after drying.
Sun-dried tomatoes are often packed in oil with herbs, extending shelf life and adding flavor.
In Italy they are called “pomodori secchi” and feature in classic dishes such as pasta with anchovies.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium contribute to normal blood pressure and cardiac function.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many dried fruits, sun-dried tomatoes contain little fat, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Many sun-dried tomatoes are salted; people with hypertension should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Sugar concentration
items.content: The high natural sugar can raise blood glucose levels; diabetics should monitor portion size.

items.title: Contamination risk if improperly dried
items.content: Insufficient drying temperatures can allow microbial growth. Purchase from reputable producers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sun-dried tomatoes can be eaten as a snack, added to salads, pastas, risottos, pizzas, omelets, or blended into sauces. Soaking them in olive oil with herbs enhances flavor and softness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sun-dried tomatoes in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. When packed in oil, keep refrigerated and use within 2‑3 weeks. Dried‑only tomatoes last up to 6 months in a dry environment. Discard if mold or off‑odors appear.

turnover-or-hot-pocket-pizza-pocket-meat.title: Turnover or Hot Pocket, Pizza Pocket, Meat

content.title: About
content.content: A turnover (also called a hot pocket or pizza pocket) is a ready‑to‑heat baked product, usually filled with meat, cheese and tomato sauce. It is a small sealed pastry with the ingredients baked inside the dough, creating a juicy and flavorful snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnovers first appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a quick way to make a hot sandwich in a microwave.
In Russia similar items are often called “pizza‑pocket” and are sold in chain fast‑food stores.
The dough is typically made from wheat flour, water, yeast and a small amount of fat, giving it a soft yet slightly crisp texture after heating.
Fillings vary from classic beef and cheese to chicken, ham, vegetables, and even vegetarian versions.
Turnovers can be stored frozen for up to 12 months without loss of quality.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The meat filling provides a substantial amount of complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Turnovers contain carbohydrates and fats, offering a quick source of energy.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Meat is rich in iron, which is essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product includes B12, B6 and niacin, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Convenience and portability
items.content: Turnovers are easy to heat in a microwave and take on the go, fitting an active lifestyle.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made items often contain a lot of salt, which may be undesirable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Meat and cheese fillings can be high in saturated fats, which should be limited in the diet.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain dairy, gluten and soy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Thermal safety
items.content: Insufficiently heated turnover may harbor pathogenic bacteria, so follow heating time recommendations.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the turnover in a microwave for 1‑2 minutes or bake in an oven until golden. Serve hot, optionally adding fresh vegetables, sauce or herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, cook immediately and do not store more than 24 hours in the refrigerator.
